C-REVIEW-CATALOG.Summary: Complete the remaining review catalogue and evaluate its usefulness on different repository types.

Goals.Goal: Trace delivery safeguards, public API access policy in source and recovery from external service failures.

Route database queries, open-source readiness, frontend communication and components, configuration, cognitive debt, implementation unification and complexity concentration to evidence-backed reviews.
Represent externally performed web assessments separately from a source review and its score.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve read-only, commit-bound inspection, stable finding ownership and previous run readability. Report absent surfaces and missing evidence distinctly. Use English and Russian topic names.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Executing the reviewed project, contacting its services, performing a web penetration test or changing repository hosting controls.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Each of the 22 user choices resolves to a section, a criterion owned by a section, or an external assessment status. The plan identifies scope, repeat results keep provenance and external evidence contributes no points.
Delivery and integration reliability have dedicated rubrics. A public API access check traces documented policy to handlers and returned fields. Conditional reviews explain applicability.
On several pinned project types, compare initial and repeated inspections with previously recorded expectations, false positives, coverage and cost. State the limits of the evidence.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Verified reports and a plan-to-actual comparison by selection.
